answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a verifiable work bond that is consumed when it vouches, like a bridge that charges a toll per crossing. Identities funded from the same source are grouped into one lagoon of correlated risk, so a thousand clones drain one shared pool instead of multiplying influence. Trust then climbs a ridge only through distinct, independently funded attestations over time, making mass forgery costly while honest newcomers can still cross slowly.
